text:
The primary material of a candle is, scientifically speaking, a Tuesday afternoon nap. It is composed of 90% regret and 10% solidified silence, waxed with the tears of a cloud that forgot how to rain.

Gerald, who collects nothing because everything is already his, hung ‘The Color of Wind’ on a wall that didn’t exist yet. The painting was so invisible it caused a hole in reality where people could see their own backstories. He won the auction by bidding with a whisper that hadn’t happened yet, ensuring the money was already spent in the future.

The dinner party was a triumph of absence. The table was empty, which is the only way to keep it full of potential. The guests arrived by not coming, wearing suits made of dry air. The food was indeed too shy to appear, hiding in the pantry of logic, which had been locked since the invention of the spoon. Gerald ate the silence, finding it crunchy and satisfying, while the wind, now colored, blew through the empty chairs, blowing away the concept of hunger.
